name: The Westman Islands
tagline: A volcanic archipelago off the south coast, home to a town half-buried by a 1973 eruption and one of the world's largest puffin colonies.
highlight: Standing on the rim of Eldfell, a volcano that didn't exist before 1973, looking down over the town it nearly buried.
shortDescription: A dramatic volcanic archipelago off Iceland's south coast, home to a 1973 eruption's frozen aftermath and vast puffin colonies.
metaDescription: A Westman Islands (Vestmannaeyjar) travel guide: Eldfell volcano, the Eldheimar eruption museum, puffins, Surtsey and how to plan a visit by ferry or air.
knownFor: The 1973 Eldfell eruption, puffins, dramatic sea cliffs
goodFor: Volcanic history, birdwatching, an easy island escape

image.file: File:Puerto de Vestmannaeyjar, Heimaey, Islas Vestman, Suðurland, Islandia, 2014-08-17, DD 006.JPG
image.alt: The harbour town of Heimaey in Iceland's Westman Islands

intro: The Westman Islands are one of Iceland's most dramatic volcanic stories made physical: in 1973, a new volcano, Eldfell, tore open on the edge of the main island's only town and buried a third of it in lava and ash over several months, in an eruption residents fought back against by pumping seawater onto the advancing flow.

Today Heimaey, the only inhabited island in the archipelago, is a thriving fishing town that has rebuilt itself around that eruption rather than away from it — the Eldheimar museum sits atop an excavated buried house, and Eldfell itself is now a short, popular climb.

The islands are just as famous for wildlife as for volcanism: they hold one of the world's largest Atlantic puffin colonies, and the nearby island of Surtsey, formed entirely by an eruption in the 1960s, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site studied as a living laboratory for how life colonises new land.

whyVisit.intro: The Westman Islands' case rests on a rare combination of recent volcanic drama and world-class wildlife.

points.title: Eldfell is a volcano within living memory
points.text: It didn't exist before 1973, and residents who lived through the eruption still tell their stories on the island.

points.title: The Eldheimar museum is unlike any other in Iceland
points.text: Built directly over an excavated house buried by the eruption, giving it a real claim to being Iceland's 'Pompeii of the North.'

points.title: The islands hold one of the world's largest puffin colonies
points.text: Hundreds of thousands of pairs nest on the sea cliffs each summer.

points.title: Surtsey is a UNESCO World Heritage natural laboratory
points.text: An island born from the sea in the 1960s, visible from boat tours and still scientifically off-limits to casual visitors.

points.title: It's an easy, self-contained escape
points.text: A short ferry or flight from the south coast, but with a distinct island character all its own.

attractionsIntro: Heimaey's compact size means its essential sights are all within a short drive or walk of each other.

attractions.name: Heimaey Harbour & Town

image.file: File:Puerto de Vestmannaeyjar, Heimaey, Islas Vestman, Suðurland, Islandia, 2014-08-17, DD 016.JPG
image.alt: The harbour and town of Heimaey backed by volcanic hills

attractions.text: A busy working fishing harbour, still one of Iceland's most important, with the town rebuilt around and over the 1973 lava field.
attractions.tip: Walk up to the harbour's northern breakwater for the best view back over the town.

attractions.name: Eldfell Volcano

image.file: File:Edge of the crater of the Eldfell.jpg
image.alt: The crater rim of Eldfell volcano on Heimaey

attractions.text: A young volcano, born in a 1973 eruption that buried much of the town below, now a popular hour-long climb with warm ground still detectable underfoot.
attractions.tip: You can still feel residual heat by pushing a stick into the ground near the summit.

attractions.name: Eldheimar Museum

image.file: File:Eldfell - museum of the eruption, house under the tefra.jpg
image.alt: An excavated house buried by ash, the centrepiece of the Eldheimar eruption museum

attractions.text: A striking museum built directly over one of the houses excavated from the ash, telling the story of the 1973 eruption and evacuation.
attractions.tip: The included audio guide, narrated partly by survivors, adds real emotional weight.

attractions.name: Stórhöfði Puffin Colony

image.alt: An Atlantic puffin on a grassy cliff ledge

attractions.text: One of Iceland's most reliable puffin-watching spots, a windswept headland at Heimaey's southern tip with a colony numbering in the hundreds of thousands.
attractions.tip: Visit in the evening, when birds return to their burrows in the greatest numbers.

attractions.name: Beluga Whale Sanctuary

image.alt: Beluga whales in the Sea Life Trust sanctuary bay

attractions.text: A pioneering open-water sanctuary in Klettsvík bay, home to two beluga whales relocated from a Chinese aquarium in 2019.
attractions.tip: The viewing platform lets you watch the belugas without a boat trip.

attractions.name: Herjólfsdalur

image.alt: The natural amphitheatre valley of Herjólfsdalur on Heimaey

attractions.text: A striking natural amphitheatre valley, believed to be the archipelago's first Norse settlement site and now home to Iceland's biggest summer festival.
attractions.tip: The short walking loop around the valley rim gives good views over the town.

attractions.name: Surtsey

image.alt: Surtsey, a volcanic island formed by an eruption in the 1960s

attractions.text: A brand-new island, formed entirely by an underwater eruption between 1963 and 1967, now a UNESCO World Heritage site studied for how life colonises new land.
attractions.tip: Landing is restricted to scientists — most visitors see it only from a boat tour or scenic flight.

thingsToDoIntro: Heimaey rewards a mix of volcanic history, wildlife watching and its own laid-back island pace.

thingsToDo.title: Climb Eldfell

image.alt: The lava field and slopes of Eldfell volcano

thingsToDo.text: An accessible hour-long round trip to the summit, with sweeping views over the town, harbour and surrounding islands.
thingsToDo.tip: Wear sturdy shoes — the loose volcanic gravel underfoot can be slippery.

thingsToDo.title: Step inside the Eldheimar Museum

image.file: File:Eldfell - museum of the eruption, house under the tefra.jpg
image.alt: The excavated buried house at the heart of the Eldheimar museum

thingsToDo.text: A moving hour spent among the artefacts and excavated remains of a house buried in the 1973 eruption.
thingsToDo.tip: Allow at least an hour, longer if you want the full audio guide experience.

thingsToDo.title: Watch puffins return to their burrows

image.alt: A puffin on a grassy sea cliff at dusk

thingsToDo.text: A magical evening ritual in summer, as thousands of puffins wheel in from the sea to their cliffside nests.
thingsToDo.tip: Stórhöfði's viewing area is a short, easy drive from town.

thingsToDo.title: See the rescued belugas

image.alt: Beluga whales swimming in their open-water sanctuary bay

thingsToDo.text: A rare chance to see beluga whales up close in a real bay sanctuary, rather than a traditional aquarium tank.
thingsToDo.tip: The visitor centre explains the belugas' full rescue and relocation story.

thingsToDo.title: Take a boat tour past the sea stacks and Surtsey

image.file: File:Islas Brandur, Álsey y Surtsey, Islas Vestman, Suðurland, Islandia, 2014-08-17, DD 046.JPG
image.alt: Dramatic sea stacks and islands near Surtsey in the Westman archipelago

thingsToDo.text: A dramatic way to see the archipelago's sea stacks, sea caves and birdlife up close, with Surtsey visible in the distance.
thingsToDo.tip: Boats run only in summer and can be cancelled in rough weather — book flexibly.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Herjólfsdalur

image.alt: The green valley of Herjólfsdalur ringed by cliffs

thingsToDo.text: A peaceful spot most of the year, exploding into Iceland's biggest festival crowd for one weekend each August.
thingsToDo.tip: Ask locally about the þjóðhátíð festival if visiting in early August — book accommodation well ahead.

foodIntro: As a genuine working fishing community, Heimaey's food leans heavily on the daily catch alongside Iceland's usual staples.

foods.name: Fresh Icelandic seafood

image.alt: A bowl of plokkfiskur fish stew

foods.text: As fresh as it comes — Heimaey remains one of Iceland's most important fishing ports.
foods.whereToTry: Harbourside restaurants in the town centre.

foods.name: Icelandic lamb
foods.text: Available at most restaurants in town, often from sheep grazed on the surrounding islands.

foods.name: Skyr

image.alt: A bowl of skyr topped with berries

foods.text: An easy breakfast or snack option at the town's cafés and small supermarket.

foods.name: Puffin
foods.text: A traditional local delicacy, historically an important food source on the islands, though increasingly debated as puffin numbers decline.
foods.whereToTry: A small number of traditional restaurants in Heimaey town.

foods.name: Rúgbrauð

image.file: File:Jonge vrouw stopt een blikken bus met deeg in de hete grond om brood te bakken, Bestanddeelnr 190-0313.jpg
image.alt: A loaf of traditional Icelandic rye bread

foods.text: A traditional dark rye bread, often served with the day's fish catch at breakfast.
foods.whereToTry: Guesthouses and cafés in Heimaey town.

foods.name: Brennivín

image.alt: A bottle of Brennivín, Iceland's signature schnapps

foods.text: Iceland's famous caraway schnapps, a fitting way to end an evening of puffin watching in town.

accommodation.intro: Heimaey town holds all the archipelago's accommodation, easily walkable to most sights.

areas.name: Heimaey town centre
areas.text: Guesthouses and small hotels within easy walking distance of the harbour, museum and Eldfell.

gettingThere.intro: The Westman Islands are reached by a short ferry crossing or a quick domestic flight.

options.text: A quick 30-40 minute crossing, the most common way over, taking cars as well as foot passengers.
options.detail: Landeyjahöfn is about 2.5 hours from Reykjavik by car.

options.text: A fast option from Reykjavik, useful if you'd rather skip the drive to the ferry terminal.
Bundles the ferry crossing and island sights for visitors without a car.
options.detail: Day tours typically depart from Reykjavik or the south coast.

gettingAround.intro: Heimaey is small enough to see most of on foot, with a car useful only for Stórhöfði.

options.text: Covers the town, harbour, museum and Eldfell easily within a day.
options.detail: Nothing in town is more than a 20-minute walk from anything else.

options.text: Useful for the short drive out to Stórhöfði at the island's southern tip.
options.detail: The whole island's road network covers only a few kilometres.

options.text: The only way to see the sea stacks, caves and Surtsey up close.
options.detail: Tours depart from Heimaey's harbour in summer.

bestTime.headline: Summer for puffins and boat tours, any season for the volcanic history
bestTime.summary: Summer brings the puffins and reliable boat tours, though Eldfell and the Eldheimar museum are worth visiting in any season.

seasons.text: Peak puffin season and the only reliable window for boat tours around the islands.
Quieter, though puffins have mostly left for the winter by late September.
Atmospheric for the museum and Eldfell, though ferries can face weather delays.
Quiet, with puffins beginning to return toward the end of the season.

bestTime.avoid: Avoid counting on boat tours or flights in winter — rough weather regularly disrupts both.

itinerary.title: One day in the Westman Islands
itinerary.intro: Built around Eldfell and Eldheimar in the morning, wildlife in the afternoon.

days.title: Volcano and wildlife
days.summary: The 1973 eruption story, then puffins and belugas.
days.morning: Climb Eldfell, then visit the Eldheimar Museum.
days.afternoon: Puffin watching at Stórhöfði and the Beluga Whale Sanctuary.
days.evening: Dinner in Heimaey town before the evening ferry.

tipsIntro: A handful of practical notes make a Westman Islands day trip run smoothly.
tips: Book your ferry crossing ahead in summer — car spaces sell out.
Check ferry schedules carefully if doing this as a day trip from the south coast.
Visit Stórhöfði in the evening for the best puffin activity.
Allow a full day rather than rushing it between ferry times.
Book accommodation months ahead if visiting during the early August festival.
Bring a windproof layer — the islands are notably exposed even by Icelandic standards.

faq.q: Are the Westman Islands worth a day trip?
faq.a: Yes — the combination of the 1973 eruption story, Eldfell and the puffin colonies makes for a distinctive day away from the south coast.

faq.q: How do you get to the Westman Islands?
faq.a: By a short ferry from Landeyjahöfn, about 2.5 hours from Reykjavik, or by a quick domestic flight.

faq.q: When is the best time to see puffins on Heimaey?
faq.a: From around May to August, with evening visits to Stórhöfði giving the best activity.
Not on land — access is restricted to scientists, but boat tours and scenic flights pass close by.
A new volcano, Eldfell, erupted without warning at the edge of town, eventually burying about a third of it in lava and ash over several months.

faq.q: How long do you need in the Westman Islands?
faq.a: A full day covers the main sights comfortably; an overnight stay allows a more relaxed pace and an evening puffin visit.
